धनञ्जय: Dhanaṃjaya m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 9, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7; also listed by Sūta among the sons of Kadrū 1. 31. 5, 2; he, among others, waits upon Varuṇa in his सभा without feeling fatigue; marked with banner (पताकिन्) and circular spots (मण्डलिन्), hooded (फणवन्त्) 2. 9. 9, 10, 11.
धनंजय: Dhanaṃjaya m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 9, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7; also listed by Sūta among the sons of Kadrū 1. 31. 5, 2; he, among others, waits upon Varuṇa in his सभा without feeling fatigue; marked with banner (पताकिन्) and circular spots (मण्डलिन्), hooded (फणवन्त्) 2. 9. 9, 10, 11.
धारण: Dhāraṇa m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 16, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7.
धूर्तक: Dhūrtaka m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Kauravya, listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacrifice of Janamejaya 1. 52. 12, 1.
धृतराष्ट्र: Dhṛtarāṣṭra m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 15, 1. A. Birth and Family: Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; also listed by Sūta among the sons of Kadrū 1. 31. 13, 2; serpents born in his कुल listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacrifice of Janame-jaya 1. 52. 13-17. B. Description: Mar-ked with jewel, स्वस्तिक, circles and कमण्-डलु; having many heads and huge shape like a mountain 5. 101. 5-7. C. Eminence: Called high-souled (महात्मन् 16. 5. 14); considered as the foremost among the snakes (धृतराष्ट्रश् च नागानां (वरः) 4. 2. 14); Uttaṅka while praising the नागस् men-tioned that when Dhṛtarāṣṭra went out two thousand eight hundred and eight snakes moved as his attendants (?) (शतान्य् अशीतिर् अष्टौ च सहस्राणि च विंशतिः सर्पाणां प्रग्रहा यान्ति धृतराष्ट्रो यद् एजति) 1. 3. 142. D. Functions and Part in the myths: One of the snakes who wait on Varuṇa in his सभा 2. 9. 9; he, along with other serpents, received the white snake issuing from the mouth of Balarāma and entering the ocean 16. 5. 14, 12; when gods prepared Śiva's chariot for his fight against the त्रिपुरस् they made its strong pole (ईषा) with ten lordly elephants chief of whom was Dhṛtarāṣṭra 8. 24. 72.
धृतराष्ट्री: Dhṛtarāṣṭrī f.: A mythical female swan (?). Daughter of Tāmrā, shining (भामिनी), she gave birth to swans (हंसस्), कल-हंसस्, and चक्रवाक birds 1. 60. 54, 56.
ध्वजविष्कम्भ: Dhvajaviṣkambha m.: A mythical bird, living in the world of Suparṇas 5. 99. 10, 1. Born in the कुल of Vainateya (Garuḍa), in the वंश of Kaśyapa; feeding on serpents; marked with श्रीवत्स, his deity is Viṣṇu; by action a Kṣatriya not obtaining Brahminhood because indulging in destroying his kinsmen 5. 99. 2-8.
धातुर्: Dhātur astra nt.: Missile (not named) of God Dhātṛ. It was known to Arjuna (and possibly to Kṛṣṇa) 6. 116. 38-39.
धौन्धुमार: Dhaundhumāra adj.: Of an उपाख्यान, so called because it describes the killing of the demon Dhundhu by king Kuvalāśva who then came to be known as Dhundhumāra (धौन्धुमारम् उपाख्यानं प्रथितं यस्य कर्मणा) 3. 195. 37, 13, 36; 3. 192. 4, 7. Described as most meritorious (धर्-मिष्ठम् इदम् आख्यानं धुन्धुमारस्य) 3. 192. 6, and holy (पुण्यम्) 3. 195. 38; it is also the praise of Viṣṇu (विष्णोः सम-नुकीर्तनम्) 3. 195. 38; one who listens to it on पर्वन् days becomes religious-minded (धर्मात्मा), gets sons, long life and fortitude; he has no fear from diseases and is free of anguish (विगतज्वरः) 3. 195. 38-39; the incident is narrated in the अध्यायस् 3. 192-195.
धनिष्ठा: Dhaniṣṭhā f. (sg., pl.): Name of a नक्षत्र। A. Computation of time began with it: When the Abhijit नक्षत्र dropped down from the sky and Indra was confused in calculating time, Brahman ordained that time (काल = युग) began with Dhaniṣṭhā, whereas for-merly it began with Rohiṇī (धनिष्ठादिस् तदा कालो ब्रह्मणा परिनिर्मितः । रोहिण्या-द्यो ऽभवत् पूर्वम्) 3. 219. 10 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 230. 10: यस्य नक्षत्रस्या-द्यक्षणे चन्द्रसूर्यगुरूणां योगस् तद् युगादिनक्षत्रम् । तच् च पूर्वं रोहिण्य् अभूत् । तदा ऽभिजित्पतनकाले तु एकन्यूनैर् अहोरात्रैर् भगणस्य भोगात् कृतयुगादि-नक्षत्रं धनिष्ठैवाभद् इत्य् अर्थः). B. Religious rites: (1) Nārada told Devakī (13. 63. 2-4) that if one, with composed mind, gave a cart, yoked with bulls and filled with garments and food (?) under the con-stellation Dhaniṣṭhā he, in the next life, instantly attained kingdom (गोप्रयुक्तं धनिष्ठासु यानं दत्त्वा समाहितः । वस्त्ररश्मिधरं सद्यः प्रेत्य राज्यम् प्रपद्यते) 13. 63. 29; (2) Yama told Śaśabindu (13. 89. 1) that if one offered a काम्य श्राद्ध under the Dhaniṣṭhā (धनि-ष्थायाम्) he obtained a share in kingdom and did not meet with difficulties 13. 89. 12.
धूमकेतु: Dhūmaketu m.: A comet; or planet Rāhu (?); according to Nī., name of a sub-ordinate planet (उपग्रह). Among the bad omens which betokened the annihilation of the Kauravas, and which were pointed out by Vyāsa to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, one was related to a very fierce comet taking hold of the Puṣya constellation (अभावं हि विशेषेष्ण कुरूणां प्रतिपश्यति । धूम-केतुर् महाघोरः पुष्यम् आक्रम्य तिष्ठति ॥ ) 6. 3. 12; (महाघोर धूम-केतु may stand for Rāhu, cf. 6. 3. 26 where a तीव्रग्रह which very probably means Rāhu, is compared to धूमकेतु; ac-cording to Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 3. 13 Dhūma-ketu is a particular उपग्रह (उपग्रह-विशेषः); he looks upon both Rāhu and Ketu as subordinate planets, cf. his Comm. on Bom. Ed. 6. 17. 2). [See Rāhu]
ध्रुव: Dhruva1 m.: Name of the polar star. A. Described as the best among the heavenly bodies (ज्योतिषां श्रेष्ठम्) 12. 326. 53; identified as the son of king Uttāna-pāda (औत्तानपाद) 13. 3. 15. B. Bad omen: Among the bad omens reported by Vyāsa to Dhṛtarāṣṭra one was related to the blazing Dhruva's movement towards left which foretold terrible happenings (ध्रुवः प्रज्वलितो घोरम् अपसव्यं प्रवर्तते) 6. 3. 16. C. Relation with Nārāyaṇa: Bhagavān (Nārāyaṇa) pointed out to Nārada that Dhruva, the best among the luminous heavenly bodies moving in the sky, was within him (ध्रुवं च ज्योतिषां श्रेष्ठं पश्य नारद खेचरं (मत्स्थं) 12. 326. 53. D. Relation with the star Viśvāmitra: Viśvāmitra, stationed between Dhruva Auttānapāda and the Brahmarṣis (the seven stars forming the constellation Ursa Major), shines constantly in the north (ध्रुवस्यौत्तानपादस्य ब्रह्मर्षीणां तथैव च । मध्ये ज्वलति यो नित्यम् उदीचीम् आश्रितो दिशम्) 13. 3. 15. E. Neg-lecting Dhruva harmful: Yājñavalkya told Janaka that those who fail to see Dhruva, having seen it once before, have only a year to live (संवत्सरवियोगस्य संभवेयुः शरीरिणः ॥ यो ऽरुन्धतीं न पश्येत दृष्टपूर्वां कदाचन । तथैव ध्रुवम् इत्य् आहुः) 12. 305. 8-9. F. Simile: All ascetics of the Naranārāyaṇāśrama (12. 126. 2) sat round king Vīradyumna as do the seven sages round Dhruva 12. 126. 25. [For Dhruva also see Section 1. 7]

Dhruva2 nt.: Designation of the four नक्षत्रस् (Rohiṇī, Pūrvā Phalgunī, Pūrvā Bhādrapadā and Pūrvāṣāḍhā). When the Pāṇḍavas decided to get the wealth of king Marutta Āvikṣita, left on the mountain Himavant, they ordered their army to march out on the day (i. e. Sunday ?, see the next) which was presided over by the Dhruva नक्षत्र (कृत्वा तु पाण्डवाः सर्वे रत्ना-हरणनिश्चयम् । सेनाम् आज्ञापयाम् आसुर् नक्षत्रे ऽहनि च ध्रुवे) 14. 62. 17 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 14. 63. 18: ध्रुवे नक्षत्रे रोहिण्याम् उत्तरात्रये च). [See Dhruva3]

Dhruva3 nt.: Designation of the day presided over by Dhruva (? i. e. Sunday ?). The Pāṇḍavas ordered their army to march out on the ध्रुव day (सेनाम् आज्ञा-पयाम् आसुर् नक्षत्रे ऽहनि च ध्रुवे) 14. 62. 17 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 14. 63. 18: अहनि वारे ध्रुवे रविवारे। But Nī.'s explanation amounts to anachronism). [See Dhruva2]
धर्मतीर्थ: Dharmatīrtha nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Described as ancient (पुरातन) 3. 82. 1, holy (पुण्य) and resorted to by Brahma-nical sages (ब्रह्मर्षिसेवित) 3. 82. 141; by bathing there one who is devoted to religion and composed (धर्मशीलः समाहितः) purifies, without doubt, his seven generations (आसप्तमं कुलं राजन् पुनीते नात्र संशयः) 3. 82. 1; by visiting Dharmatīrtha one undoubtedly obtains the fruit of a Vājapeya sacrifice 3. 82. 141.
धर्मपृष्ठ: Dharmapṛṣṭha nt.: Name of a sacred place. Dharma is always present there (यत्र धर्मो महाराज नित्यम् आस्ते); by visiting this place one who has a composed mind (समाहितः) gets the fruit of a horse sacrifice 3. 82. 87.
धर्मारण्य: Dharmāraṇya nt.: Name of a sacred forest. Described as a favourite of gods (सुरैर् वृतम्) 13. 151. 23; lake Brahmasaras is situated in it (ततो ब्रह्मसरो गच्छेद् धर्मारण्योपशोभितम्) 3. 82. 74; 13. 26. 55; finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 23, 2; (also used as a general term for holy groves 14. 96. 13 (दर्मारण्यानि); qualifies Kaṇvāśrama 3. 80. 65 and Daṇḍa-kāraṇya 3. 261. 43, 40).
धारा: Dhārā f.: Name of a तीर्थ। Described as destroying all sin (सर्व-पापप्रणाशिनी); by bathing there one does not grieve (न शोचति) 3. 82. 22.
धूतपापा: Dhūtapāpā f.: Name of a river. One of the rivers listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 17, 13; all the rivers listed here are said to be the mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
धूमत्या: Dhūmatyā f.: Name of a river. One of the rivers listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 23, 13; all the rivers listed here are said to be mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
धूमावती: Dhūmāvatī f.: Name of a sacred place (or of a goddess ?) By fasting there for three nights one undoubtedly gets the desired objects; to the right side of the goddess there, there is a sacred place called Rathāvarta (धूमावतीं ततो गच्छेत् … ॥ देव्यास् तु दक्षिणार्धेन रथावर्तो नराधिप) 3. 82. 20-21.
धेनुक: Dhenuka nt., Denukā f.: Name of a sacred place. Described as famous in the world (लोक-विश्रुता) 3. 82. 76; one should stay there for a night and give as a gift a तिलधेनुका; the gift cleanses the giver of all sins and he goes to the world of Soma (एकरात्रोषितो राजन् प्रयच्छेत् तिलधेनुकाम्) 3. 82. 76 (“In imitation of the gift of the cow gifts of certain articles were made and they are also described as धेनुस्” P. V. Kane Hist. of Dharma. II. II p. 880; cf. Mbh. 13. 70. 37-40); Pulastya told Bhīṣma that a Kapilā cow with her calf roamed near this place on the moun-tain; the signs of their hoof-prints are seen even now; if one touches the dust from those prints (तेषूपस्पृश्य राजेन्द्र पदेषु नृप-सत्तम), whatever unholy deed (अशुभं कर्म) one may have committed that is destroyed 3. 82. 77-78; Mṛtyu conceived as a maiden, unwilling to carry out Brahman's instruction to deprive the subjects of their lives, repaired to Dhenuka without agreeing to carry out the instruction, and practised severe austerities 12. 250. 15-16 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 258. 15: धेनुकं गोतीर्थं मायान्तर्वर्ति).
ध्रुवद्वार: Dhruvadvāra nt.: Name of a place. The place where Gaṅgā fell on the earth (?); Nārada once went there to take bath (ध्रुवद्वारभवां गङ्गां जगामा-वततार च) 12. 221. 6.
धृतराष्ट्रस्य: Dhṛtarāṣṭrasya āśramaḥ1 m.: An आश्रम established by Dhṛtarāṣṭra at Kuru-kṣetra; also called Kurukṣetrāśrama (15. 29. 21). A. Location: At Kurukṣetra, on the other bank of Yamunā at some distance from the river; when Dhṛtarāṣṭra, with Gāndhārī and Kuntī, left Hāstinapura he reached Kurukṣetra (कुरुक्षेत्रं जगाम सः) 15. 25. 8; when Yudhiṣṭhira, with his brothers and wife, went to meet Dhṛtarāṣṭra in his आश्रम he had to cross the river Yamunā (ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा कुरुक्षे-त्रम् अवातरत् । … उत्तीर्य यमुनां … स ददर्शाश्रमं दूरात् … धृतराष्ट्रस्य) 15. 30. 16-17; 15. 31. 6; it was situated near the आश्रम of Śatayūpa 15. 25. 9, 12; 15. 30. 17; also not far from Bhāgīrathī 15. 25. 8; 15. 39. 18, 21; 15. 40. 4. B. Description: Solitary (शून्य) 15. 31. 3; resorted to by Siddhas and Cāraṇas (सिद्धचारणसेवीत) 15. 31. 20; in the precincts of the आश्रम there were fire altars with burning sacrifi-cial fires attended to by sages who had taken bath and who gave offerings in the fire (ददर्श तत्र वेदीश् च संप्रज्वलितपाव-काः । कृताभिषेकैर् मुनिभिर् आहुताग्निभिर् उपस्थिताः । ) 15. 34. 7; the fire altars were scattered with forest flowers, were full of smoke issuing from clarified butter, were endowed with Brahmanical lustre, and were surrounded by hosts of sages (वानेय-पुष्पनिकरैर् आज्यधूमोद्गमैर् अपि । ब्रा-ह्मेण वपुषा युक्ता युक्ता मुनिगणैश् च ताः) 15. 34. 8; the hermitage was full of deer (मृगगणाकीर्ण) 15. 31. 3; herds of deer moved about undistractedly near the आश्रम and singing birds flew over it fearlessly; notes of peacocks, Dātyūhas, sweet sounds of cuckoos and sounds of Vedic recitations of Brāhmaṇas could be heard at different places (मृगयूथैर् अनुद्विग्नैस् तत्र तत्र समाश्रितैः । अशङ्कितैः पक्षिगणैः प्रगी-तैर् इव च प्रभो ॥ केकाभिर् नीलकण्ठा-नां दात्यूहानां च कूजितैः । कोकिलानां च कुहरैः शुभैः श्रुतिमनोहरैः ॥ ) 15. 34. 9-10; beautified by large number of banana trees (कदलीवनशोभित) 15. 31. 3; there were large baskets for collecting fruits and roots (फलमूलसमुद्वाहैर् महद्-भिश् चोपशोभितम्) 15. 34. 11. C. Epic events: (1) In Kurukṣetra, Dhṛtarāṣṭra first reached the आश्रम of the royal sage Śatayūpa; he lived in this आश्रम and after he was initiated by Vyāsa in his own आश्रम and was instructed by Śatayūpa in the way of the life of a forest-dweller, Dhṛtarāṣṭra established another आश्रम for himself, Gāndhārī and Kuntī for the pra-ctice of austerities (ययौ व्यासाश्रमं तदा । … स दिक्षां तत्र संप्राप्य राजा … शतयूपाश्रमे तस्मिन् निवासम् अकरोत् तदा ॥ तस्मै सर्वं विधिं राजन् राजा-चख्यौ महामतिः । आरण्यकम् … एवं स तपसा राजा धृतराष्ट्रो महामनाः । योजयाम् आस चात्मानम्) 15. 25. 11-14; (2) Yudhiṣṭhira, desirous of meeting Dhṛtarāṣṭra and others, ordered his carriages and the rest to move to Kuru-kṣetrāśrama (निर्यान्तु … कुरुक्षेत्राश्रमं प्रति) 15. 29. 19-21; (3) When Yudhiṣṭhira, with his brothers and Draupadī, reached Kurukṣetra and crossed the river Yamunā he saw from a distance the आश्रमस् of Śatayūpa and Dhṛtarāṣṭra (स ददर्शाश्र-मं दूराद् राजर्षेस् तस्य धीमतः । शत-यूपस्य कौरव्य धृतराष्ट्रस्य चैव ह ॥ ) 15. 30. 16-17; the Pāṇḍavas got down from their chariots and went on foot (पदातयः) to the आश्रम of Dhṛtarāṣṭra (पाण्डवाः … अभिजग्मुर् नरपतेर् आश्रमम्) 15. 31. 1; आश्रमं ते ततो जग्मुर् धृतराष्ट्रस्य पाण्डवाः 15. 31. 3; when Dhṛtarāṣṭra, who had gone to bathe in Yamunā and to fetch flowers, returned to the आश्रम along with the Pāṇḍavas who had rushed there to meet him, he sat down in the आश्रम with the Pāṇḍavas and the ascetics who had gathered to see the Pāṇḍavas 15. 31. 6-8, 20; 15. 32. 1-2; when the ascetics and others had left the आश्रम (आश्रम-मण्डलम्) Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Yudhiṣṭhira his कुशल 15. 32. 18; when Vidura saw from a distance some people seated in the आश्रम he wanted to go away from it 15. 33. 18; the Pāṇḍavas lived in the आश्रम for that night 15. 33. 35-37; 15. 34. 1, 4; next morning Yudhiṣṭhira and the rest went around to see the precincts of the आश्रम (ददर्शाश्रममण्डलम्) 15. 34. 5-6; after finishing their round (परीत्याश्रम-मण्डलम्) Yudhiṣṭhira gave many kinds of gifts to the ascetics 15. 34. 12-15; the Pāṇḍavas lived in the forest near the आश्रम for a month 15. 36. 6-7; (4) While the Pāṇḍavas were still In the आश्रम, Vyāsa, by the strength of his austerities, showed them the miracle, promised before, on the river Bhāgīrathī which was not done by any great sage before (न कृतं यत् पुरा कैश्चित् कर्म लोके महर्षिभिः । आश्चर्यभूतं तपसः फलं संदर्श-यामि वः) 15. 35. 24; (वसत्सु पण्डु-पुत्रेषु सर्वेष्व् आश्रममण्डले । यत् तद् आश्चर्यम् इति वै करिष्यामीत्य् उवाच ह । व्यासः) 15. 36. 2-3; (the miracle is describ-ed in 15. 40-41); (5) After witnessing the miracle, Dhṛtarāṣṭra returned to the आश्रम; Vyāsa instructed him there and asked him to give permission to the Pāṇḍa-vas to return to Hāstinapura 15. 44. 2, 5-11, 21, 52. D. Simile: The आश्रम filled with people curious to see it compared with the sky full of stars (आश्रमम् … दिदृक्षुभिः समाकीर्णं नभस् तारागणैर् इव) 15. 31. 20.

Dhṛtarāṣṭrasya āśramaḥ2 m.: आश्रम of Dhṛtarāṣṭra. When Dhṛtarāṣṭra went from Kuru-kṣetra to Gaṅgādvāra he established there another आश्रम on the river Gaṅgā 15. 45. 10; once, when Dhṛtarāṣṭra had bathed in Gaṅgā and was facing his आश्रम strong wind blew and a great forest fire suddenly arose in which Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gāndhārī and Kuntī were burnt to ashes (ततः कदा-चिद् गङ्गायाः कच्छे स नृपसत्तमः । गङ्गायाम् आप्लुतो धिमान् आश्रमाभिमुखो ऽभवत् । अथ वायुः समुद्भूतो दावाग्निर् अभवन् महान्) 15. 45. 18-19, 31.
धौम्याश्रम: Dhaumyāśrama m.: Hermitage of Dhaumya. Situated near the तीर्थ Utkocaka (तत उत्कोचकं तीर्थं गत्वा धौम्या-श्रमं तु ते); as advised by the Gan-dharva Citraratha, the Pāṇḍavas reached the आश्रम of Dhaumya and chose Dhau-mya as their Purohita; Dhaumya received the Pāṇḍavas in his आश्रम by offering them water to wash feet and fruits and roots and by agreeing to be their Purohita (तान् धौम्यः प्रतिजग्राह … । पाद्येन फलमूलेन पौरोहित्येन चैव ह ॥ ) 1. 174. 6-7.
धृतिमत्: Dhṛtimant nt. (sg.): Name of a Varṣa. Fifth Varṣa in the list of the seven Varṣas of Kuśadvīpa (धृतिमत् पञ्चमं वर्षं … सप्तैते वर्षपुञ्जकाः) 6. 13. 13; for the description of the people of Dhṛtimant (6. 13. 14-15) see Audbhida.
धृतिमन्त्: Dhṛtimant nt. (sg.): Name of a Varṣa. Fifth Varṣa in the list of the seven Varṣas of Kuśadvīpa (धृतिमत् पञ्चमं वर्षं … सप्तैते वर्षपुञ्जकाः) 6. 13. 13; for the description of the people of Dhṛtimant (6. 13. 14-15) see Audbhida.
ध्वजिन्युत्सवसंकेत: Dhvajinyutsavasaṃketa m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. One of the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa listed by Saṃjaya (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा … ) 6. 10. 56; (ध्वजिन्युत्सवसं-केताः) 6. 10. 59; (Related to the Utsava-saṃketas ?)
